claim.pdf_says: 10) If more than one integer-1 or integer-2 operand is specified ... c) The occurrences of integer-1, if present, shall be in ascending numerical order. ... 12) Identifier-1 shall be described in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section as an elementary unsigned integer data item.  (all hyphens printed as the ordinary hyphen U+002D, as everywhere else in the document)
claim.markdown_says: integer‑1 / integer‑2 / Identifier‑1 / working‑storage / local‑storage  (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 19250, 19256, 19264 encode the hyphen as U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN instead of U+002D)
claim.why_it_matters: These are COBOL metavariable and section names. Encoded with U+2011 they are no longer byte-identical to 'integer-1', 'Identifier-1', 'working-storage', 'local-storage' as spelled in the surrounding text and everywhere else in the standard, so grep/citation tooling that searches for the operand names silently misses these three general rules of 13.18.35.3. The artifact is sporadic (107 occurrences on 38 lines file-wide), not a deliberate typographic convention.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, and every quantitative assertion in the claim reproduced exactly. (1) MARKDOWN SIDE: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 19250 = '10) If more than one integer\u20111 or integer\u20112 operand is specified, ...', line 19256 = 'c) The occurrences of integer\u20111, if present, ...', line 19264 = '12) Identifier\u20111 shall be described in the file, working\u2011storage, local\u2011storage, or linkage section ...'. A file-wide Unicode-category Pd census gives U+002D x47171, U+2014 x1040, U+2011 x107, U+2013 x104 -- exactly the claimed 107 occurrences on exactly the claimed 38 lines. (2) PDF SIDE, and this is the part the claim asserted but did not prove: the page-451 text layer is glyph-code obfuscated (no ToUnicode map), so no codepoint can be read from it naively and, critically, U+002D and U+2011 are glyph-identical in this typeface, so the 300-dpi render CANNOT discriminate them by eye. I decoded the subset encoding by known-plaintext alignment instead. In the PDF the hyphen is ONE glyph code, U+01E6: it follows 'integer' 157/157 times and precedes 'storage' 17/17 times across a 190-page sample spanning pages 200-260, 400-470 and 900-960, including all five hyphens on page 451 itself. The PDF draws no distinction anywhere. (3) INTERNAL-INCONSISTENCY PROOF, decisive on its own: the markdown splits that single source character two ways. The immediately adjacent pages 450, 452 and 453 -- same 13.18.35 LINE clause, same operands -- spell 'integer-1' and 'integer-2' with ordinary U+002D, while page 451 spells them U+2011. Eight lines mix BOTH encodings within a single line; line 31381 (page 773) reads '32) If FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO Is specified, the content of identifier\u201114 is set as follows:' -- U+002D and U+2011 in one sentence -- and the page-773 text layer shows all 13 occurrences of 'dentifier' followed by the same U+01E6, so the PDF distinguishes nothing. The U+2011 runs cluster in contiguous blocks (17910-17933, 19250-19264, 19924-19928, 29504-29530, 31381-31397, 34863-34867), the signature of per-chunk transcription drift rather than a source property. (4) VISUAL: in the render I see ordinary short hyphens in 'integer-1', 'integer-2', 'Identifier-1', 'working-storage' and 'local-storage', plainly shorter than the en dash printed in rule 11 ('MINUS and - are synonyms') -- they are hyphens, not dashes; only the glyph-code analysis can separate 002D from 2011. Rejection tests all fail to bite: no text is missing, the difference is not page furniture / line wrapping / line-break hyphenation / layout formatting but a character-identity change inside words, and neither source is misquoted. Human-readable meaning is indeed unchanged, which is why cosmetic is the right severity -- but the transcription is not byte-faithful to its source and is inconsistent with itself, and in a standard whose identifiers are hyphen-joined, exact-string search for the operand names silently skips these rules. That is a genuine, mechanically verified, repairable transcription defect.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, correctly located and correctly counted, but the evidence is stated one step too strongly and the scope is stated one step too narrowly. (a) EVIDENCE: 'the PDF prints U+002D' cannot be established by looking -- U+002D and U+2011 render as the same glyph, and the ISO text layer is obfuscated. What is establishable, and what I established, is that the PDF encodes ONE hyphen character throughout (subset glyph U+01E6: 157/157 after 'integer', 17/17 before 'storage', over a 190-page sample), and the markdown renders that one character as U+002D 47171 times and as U+2011 107 times. The defect is the transcription's inconsistency against a uniform source, not a provable 2011-for-002D substitution. (b) The strongest proof is internal, and the claim omits it: adjacent pages 450/452/453 spell the same 13.18.35 operands 'integer-1'/'integer-2' with U+002D while page 451 uses U+2011, and 8 lines carry both encodings within one line -- e.g. line 31381 'FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO' (U+002D) beside 'identifier\u201114' (U+2011), where the page-773 text layer shows the identical glyph for both. (c) SCOPE: this is not a page-451 finding. Page 451 is 3 of 38 affected lines; the repair is a single global normalization of U+2011 -> U+002D across all 107 occurrences (leaving U+2013 and U+2014 alone, which are genuine en/em dashes such as the '-' printed in GR 11 on this page), and the reconciliation ledger should carry it once at file scope rather than 13 times per page. (d) Severity cosmetic is correct: no rule's meaning changes; the impact is confined to byte-exact grep and citation tooling.
